after_return_text: These are learning questions, not substitutes for the individual sign descriptions. A warning of children, for example, does not assign a new numerical speed by itself; your speed must still allow safe control and a response to foreseeable hazards. A posted maximum speed is a ceiling, not a demand to maintain that speed. Road Signs Regulation, chapter 2 · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§14–15 | Requirements. B1 means yield to vehicles on the crossing road or route. Make that intention clear early and proceed only without danger or obstruction. B2 requires a stop before entering the crossing road or track area. Stop at the stop line; without one, stop immediately before the signal or before entering the crossing road or track area, as applicable. A rolling pause does not meet a stop duty. Road Signs Regulation, B1–B2 · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§5 and 19 | Yield and stop Signs and markings are labelled teaching counterparts. These examples do not establish their position in a particular road scene. | Enlarge Give way image | Yield to vehicles on the crossing road or route. With a distance or stop-ahead panel, this can instead be advance information. Inverted triangular give-way sign. | Enlarge Stop image | Make a complete stop before entering the crossing road, route or track area. Use the stop line; without one, apply the prescribed stopping position. Red octagon bearing STOP. | Enlarge Stop line image | This identifies where to stop when a sign or signal requires it. The line alone does not create a universal stop duty. Wide transverse white stop line.
